Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
articles.abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

articles.title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
articles.abstract: Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

articles.title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
articles.abstract: Abstract Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

articles.title: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
articles.abstract: Abstract Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

articles.title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
Scalable 3D hybrid integrated photonic computing chiplets
Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
articles.abstract: Abstract The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp 2 -hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants

Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
articles.abstract: Abstract Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

articles.title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
articles.abstract: Abstract Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.

articles.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
articles.abstract: Abstract Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort ( N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) ( N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, P log-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, p log-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c ( p AUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant ( p = 0.035) and age-related ( p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

articles.title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures

Artificial
Intelligence for Methane Detection: From
Continuous Monitoring to Verified Mitigation
articles.abstract: Abstract Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, responsible for roughly 30% of warming since preindustrial times. A small number of large point sources account for a disproportionate share of emissions, creating an opportunity for substantial reductions by targeting relatively few sites. Detection and attribution of large emissions at scale for notifying asset owners remains challenging. Here, we introduce MARS-S2L, a machine learning model that detects methane emissions in publicly available multispectral satellite imagery. Trained on a manually curated data set of over 80,000 images, the model provides high-resolution detections every 2 days, enabling facility-level attribution and identifying 78% of plumes with an 8% false-positive rate at 697 previously unseen sites. Deployed operationally, MARS-S2L has issued 2,776 notifications to stakeholders in 25 countries, enabling verified, permanent mitigation of six persistent emitters, including a superemitter in Algeria that had been releasing approximately 27,500 tonnes of methane annually for at least a decade and a previously unknown emitter in Libya first identified by MARS-S2L. These results demonstrate a scalable pathway from satellite detection to quantifiable methane mitigation.

articles.title:
Using Street View
and Remote Sensing Imagery to Estimate
NO2 and PM2.5 Concentrations for the Continental
US
articles.abstract: Abstract Land use regression (LUR) models are widely used for estimating fine-scale ambient air quality. Street view and remote sensing imagery are emerging sources to measure built environment features which may enhance traditional LUR predictors and further improve model performance. In this study, we investigate using various combinations of street view and remote sensing derived features to develop national annual NO2 and PM2.5 machine learning models (2007–2020). Predictors in our models include: (1) Google Street View (GSV) imagery derived semantic features, (2) satellite-based aerosol estimates, and (3) Landsat-derived spectral indices and elevation. Full models combining all predictors achieved the best model performance, with random 10-fold cross validation R2 values of 0.92 for NO2 and 0.75 for PM2.5. Models incorporating GSV-derived features generally achieve enhanced model fit. Beyond conventional internal model evaluation, we examined how different predictors impact the spatial patterns of model prediction surfaces. GSV-informed models yielded a wider range of model estimates and better captured intraurban air pollution variability─a finding confirmed by external validation using independent mobile monitoring and calibrated PurpleAir measurements. Our results highlight the potential of street-view imagery to characterize fine-scale spatial gradients in air pollution and thus support more spatially resolved exposure assessment.

articles.title: Mechanisms and Prediction of Microcystis Removal by Sediment Resuspension in Drinking-Water Reservoirs
articles.abstract: Abstract Microcystis blooms threaten drinking-water quality, yet sustainable in situ controls are needed. A survey of 43 drinking-water reservoirs in eastern China and the Tibetan Plateau found moderate- to high-intensity blooms in 26% of the reservoirs. We evaluated sediment resuspension (SR) as a nature-based intervention. Experiments with ten sediments showed that Microcystis removal (35.0% ± 14.3%) coincided with declining dissolved Fe and Al. Experiments and scanning electron microscopy–energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM–EDS) identified Fe/Al-mediated flocculation and settling, rather than particles alone, as the primary short-term removal pathway. Sediment composition regulated reactive Fe/Al supply and utilization: maximum Fe+Al removal increased with active Fe+Al content (R2 = 0.88, p < 0.001), whereas flocculation effectiveness declined as the fine-particle fraction (<63 μm) increased (R2 = 0.67, p < 0.03). We developed a sediment-property-based model from these relationships. Across more than 30 reservoirs in eastern China, predicted Microcystis removal averaged (1.37 ± 1.97) × 108 cells L–1. In a Microcystis-dominated reservoir, predicted and field-fitted removal rates differed by 6%. Observations from five filamentous-cyanobacteria-dominated reservoirs suggested Fe/Al-related flocculation may also aid removal of other taxa. This study provides a mechanistic, predictive basis for evaluating SR in bloom management.

articles.title:
Laboratory and Field
Investigation of Amines in Automotive
Brake Wear Particles
articles.abstract: Abstract Nonexhaust vehicle emissions (brake wear, tire wear, and road dust) now dominate particulate matter (PM) sources in urban environments as tailpipe emissions continue to decline. Among these, brake wear particles (BWPs) remain under-characterized, particularly their organic composition. This study investigates the formation and atmospheric relevance of amines released during the thermal degradation of phenolic resin, the primary binder in brake pads. Controlled brake dynamometer and phenolic-resin thermal degradation experiments were performed together with field measurements adjacent to two Southern California freeways (I-5, Santa Ana, and I-710, Long Beach). High-resolution mass spectrometry analysis revealed the prevalence of nitrogen-containing compounds across all data sets with dicyclohexylamine (C12H23N; DCHA) consistently detected in laboratory and ambient particles. DCHA concentrations in laboratory particles ranged from 0.08 to 1.6 ng/μg across brake pad types and resin conditions. DCHA was measured in air sampled onto filters at levels ranging from 2.1 ± 1.6 pg m–3 (Santa Ana) to 3.5 ± 1.7 pg m–3 (Long Beach). Ambient levels of DCHA correlated with near-road NO and brake-associated metals (Fe, Ba), suggesting a possible link between its emission and braking activity. These findings identify brake wear as a previously under-recognized source of DCHA and related organic nitrogen compounds, often associated primarily with tire wear emissions.

articles.title:
Biomass-Derived
Supramolecular Living Hydrogels for
Adaptive Dye Wastewater Remediation
articles.abstract: Abstract Dye wastewater from textile, leather, and paper industries poses a persistent threat to aquatic ecosystems owing to its chemical recalcitrance and potential toxicity. Microalgae provide a sustainable strategy for dye bioremediation through synergistic bioaccumulation and biodegradation. However, these microbes suffer from limited tolerance to the complex composition of dye wastewater and are difficult to recycle after treatment. Here, we report retrievable living microalgae-loaded polysaccharide hydrogel networks coated with tannic acid (MPH@TA) for efficient purification of wastewater containing diverse dyes. The flexible supramolecular networks containing Chlorella pyrenoidosa create a protective microenvironment that supports robust microalgal growth and efficient dye removal while reducing the leakage of microalgae. Notably, MPH@TA achieves removal efficiencies of 97.7% and 94.5% for 100 mg L–1 malachite green and reactive red, respectively, highlighting its implementation for both cationic and anionic dyes. The living MPH@TA system enables facile recyclability and effective treatment of complex real dye wastewater. Transcriptomic analysis shows that MPH@TA modulates the antioxidant defense, redox metabolism, and respiratory energy supply of microalgae, thereby enhancing microalgal tolerance and biotransformation of dye molecules. This work not only provides a simple yet efficient strategy for water purification but also advances insights into microbe–material hybrid interactions for engineered living materials.

articles.title:
Revisiting
the Climate
Benefits Provided by Wood through
Future-Oriented Material and Energy Displacement
articles.abstract: Abstract Displacement factors (DFs) quantify climate benefits of wood-based products relative to non-wood alternatives. Existing DFs are typically static whereas economy-wide decarbonization motivates a forward-looking assessment. Previous work focuses on semifinished materials and lacks harmonized, transparent modeling. This study provides an open-access, unit-process-based database of future-oriented DFs for 81 wood-product-material-variants across six end-use categories. It uses time-explicit life cycle assessment (LCA), which links processes to the technology landscape as they occur, under three decarbonization scenarios for 2020–2070. Wood-based products showed positive DFs in 2020, with weighted averages from near-zero for furniture to 1.04 kg C/kg C for chemicals and textiles, though lower than previous estimates. DFs declined over time for all products except chemicals, most steeply under climate-ambitious scenarios. Wood sustained the highest benefit in the least ambitious scenario. The decline was driven by faster decarbonization of non-wood products that contain proportionally more fossil-intensive components. Time-explicit LCA yielded lower DFs for long-lived products as end-of-life processes were assigned to more decarbonized future years, an effect not captured by conventional or prospective LCA. Energy-related DFs approached near-zero by 2070. The findings support redirecting wood flows from energy toward long-lived material applications and caution against harvest intensification justified on displacement arguments alone.

articles.title:
Complementary Mechanisms
for Fe(II)-Mediated Nickel
and Cobalt Release from Laterites
articles.abstract: Abstract Nickel (Ni) and cobalt (Co) mining must increase as renewable energy generation and energy storage technologies expand. Most of the world’s Ni is found in laterite deposits, but the processing of these ores is costly, energy-intensive, and damaging to the environment. Here, we present a novel ferrous leaching approach that operates at ambient conditions (22 °C, pH 7.5) to recover Ni and Co from four lateritic domains from the Barnes Hill Deposit in Tasmania, Australia. Ni and Co K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) shows that most of the Ni is bound in iron (Fe) (oxyhydr)oxide and silicate phases, whereas Co is predominantly associated with manganese (Mn) oxide minerals. Under optimal leach conditions, up to 38% of Ni and approximately 100% of Co are recovered. XAS analysis on the leached samples shows that Co (and Mn) release occurs by Fe(II)-induced reductive dissolution of Mn oxides. In the case of Ni, 57Fe-isotope tracer results suggest Fe(II)-catalyzed mineral recrystallization is repartitioning solid-phase Ni to a more labile form, while Ni hosted in silicate phases such as serpentine can also be extracted with a mild acid wash. Our results demonstrate that ferrous leaching is highly effective at solubilizing Co (and Ni) and thus may be a viable strategy for processing Co-rich laterites as well as metal-bearing Mn oxides such as deep-sea nodules and crusts.

articles.title:
When Selectivity
Is Not Enough: Product-Centered Metrics
for Environmental Separations
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanofiltration (NF) has traditionally been evaluated through the lens of water production, utilizing water/solute selectivity as the primary performance metric. As NF increasingly targets selective solute fractionation for resource recovery, the focus has shifted toward solute/solute selectivity. However, relying solely on selectivity can be fundamentally misleading because it frequently misaligns with practical process objectives. Furthermore, evaluating materials strictly based on instantaneous selectivity can potentially obscure the true process-level viability. This Perspective redefines performance evaluation by establishing a unified, product-centered framework applicable across three distinct separation scenarios: recovering the permeate, the retentate, or both streams as valuable products. To this end, we introduce a new framework based on the recovery-retention diagram to evaluate generic binary separations. This framework demonstrates how separation outcomes are intrinsically governed by both membrane performance and feed composition, which can be captured by the separation trajectory. Ultimately, transitioning from a purely selectivity-based evaluation framework to a product-centered one bridges the critical gap between bench-scale material discovery and scalable process engineering.

articles.title:
Heatwaves Shift
Ozone Formation toward Greater NOx Sensitivity through
Enhanced VOC Availability and Radical
Cycling
articles.abstract: Abstract Heatwaves aggravate surface ozone (O3) pollution, yet their impacts on O3 formation sensitivity and precursor control effectiveness remain insufficiently resolved. We integrate reanalysis data, ground-based observations, satellite retrievals, meteorological normalization, and observation-based modeling to elucidate the effects of heatwaves on O3 concentrations, precursor availability, radical chemistry, and O3 formation sensitivity in an emission-intensive urban basin. Heatwave frequency, duration, and cumulative intensity during April–September increased by factors of 2.1–3.2 in 2015–2024 relative to 1975–2014. Heatwaves not only enhanced O3 formation but also reshaped O3 formation sensitivity by increasing BVOCs and AVOCs possibly associated with fuel evaporation and solvent use, elevating ROx levels, and strengthening the oxidation of NO by peroxy radicals. Observation-based modeling revealed a shift from VOC-limited toward transitional regimes in urban Chengdu during the more strongly heatwave-affected Augusts, while satellite diagnostics provided supporting evidence for changes toward greater NOx sensitivity in parts of the basin. Sensitivity simulations further demonstrated that O3 formation sensitivity to NOx increased systematically with rising temperature and that sufficient NOx reductions effectively weakened the temperature sensitivity of O3 formation in Chengdu. These results support climate-adaptive O3 mitigation combining routine VOC–NOx controls with stronger reductions in NOx and temperature-sensitive AVOC emissions during heatwaves.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information

Heatwaves Trigger
Nonlinear Rises in Nonmethane Hydrocarbons
articles.abstract: Abstract Urban heatwaves intensify ozone and particulate pollution by accelerating volatile organic compound (VOC) oxidation in the presence of nitrogen oxides (NOx). However, the temperature dependence of anthropogenic nonmethane hydrocarbons (NMHCs) remains poorly constrained and may become strongly nonlinear under extreme heat. The temperature response of anthropogenic VOC emissions depends on species-specific physicochemical properties. Here, we show that anthropogenic NMHC concentrations measured in Guangzhou, China, exhibit two distinct temperature thresholds at 26.5 °C (associated with the dew point) and near 30 °C (associated with an effective volatility threshold), above which concentrations increase abruptly. Using high-resolution observations, statistical classification, and thermodynamic simulations, we show that these thresholds arise from coupled volatility and chemical-reactivity effects that link phase behavior to atmospheric chemical loss. Chemical depletion accelerates with warming but exhibits diminishing marginal sensitivity, while ambient NMHCs volatilize in three hierarchical batches ordered by boiling point. These nonlinear concentration responses are not captured by traditional steady-state emission parametrizations that assume simple linear temperature scaling. Incorporating threshold-based volatilization behavior into urban chemistry models should improve predictions of ozone formation and particulate pollution during heatwaves and under future climate warming.

articles.title:
Foliar CeO2 Nanoparticles Mitigate Cadmium
Phytotoxicity in Strawberry by Suppressing Cd Accumulation and Activating
a Secondary Metabolite Defense Network
articles.abstract: Abstract Atmospheric cadmium (Cd) deposition threatens food safety, yet how beneficial nanoparticles (NPs) augment plant tolerance to heavy metal stress remains poorly understood. Here, we dissected the protective mechanisms of foliar-applied CeO2 NPs against Cd toxicity in strawberries by integrating physiology, transcriptomics, and metabolomics. Foliar Cd exposure caused significant Cd accumulation in leaves (9.77 mg/kg dry weight) and translocation to roots and fruits (0.964 and 0.292 mg/kg dry weight). This resulted in 70.5% inhibition of photosynthesis and 20.6% and 29.0% increases in MDA and GSH relative to those of the control, indicating photosynthetic damage and oxidative stress. Coapplied CeO2 NPs counteracted this phytotoxicity by reducing leaf Cd by 23.4% and lowering MDA contents by 16.8%, consequently restoring photosynthesis by 2.30-fold. Multiomics unveiled the molecular basis of this biostimulation. Specifically, CeO2 NPs upregulated gene expression involved in hormone signaling and terpenoid biosynthesis (e.g., EIN3, JAZ, MVD, and DXS) and levels of flavonoids, phenol ethers, and l-glutamate, which support the oxidative stress prevention and plant defense. Moreover, redox homeostasis, associated with these genes and metabolites alongside Cd accumulation, regulated photosynthesis (effect size: −0.604). This work suggests a mechanistic dual-action hypothesis and positions CeO2 NPs as a sustainable nanostrategy for safeguarding crops against atmospheric heavy metal stress.

articles.title:
Redox
Perturbations
Promote Oxidative and Cometabolic
Reaction Networks for Enhanced Organic Micropollutant Removal in Activated
Sludge
articles.abstract: Abstract Understanding how redox conditions shape enzyme expression and micropollutant transformation in activated sludge remains a key challenge. Here, we show that engineered redox perturbation enriches enzymatic guilds that shape not only the extent of organic micropollutant (OMP) removal but the type and coupling of reaction pathways. Dynamic oxic–anoxic cycling at 2 or 7 mg/L dissolved oxygen, with nominal 3- or 6 min periods, restructured enzyme expression and expanded transformation chemistry beyond that of steady aeration. Integrating SWATH-MS metaproteomics with Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) paired mass distance (PMD) reactomics across 30 OMPs, we resolved condition-specific enzyme upregulation: OxyR-associated catalase-peroxidase induction (EC 1) under high-DO cycling tracked oxygenation-type PMDs ([+O], [+2O], [+3O]), whereas transferase (EC 2) and hydrolase (EC 3) upregulation tracked methylation, acylation, and bond-cleavage signatures. Perturbation significantly upregulated 18 PMD types over continuous aeration, expanded OMP reaction networks, and drove removal gains up to 63% for macrolides and 49% for nitrogen heterocycles, whereas benzotriazole, diclofenac, and carbendazim declined, possibly through NADPH competition. Class-level guild analysis linked Proteobacterial and Nitrospira enzymes to functional-group-selective transformations, with perturbation mainly redistributing each class’s contribution to shared enzyme pools. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for tailoring redox regimes in existing systems to enhance OMP removal.

articles.title: Issue Editorial Masthead

Humic
and Fulvic Acids Elicit Distinct Multi-Organ
and Microbial Responses after Chronic Oral Exposure
articles.abstract: Abstract Humic acid (HA) and fulvic acid (FA) are major constituents of natural organic matter (NOM) that can exhibit dynamic supramolecular and colloidal organization in aqueous environments. Given the widespread occurrence of NOM in environmental waters and that untreated natural water can represent a chronic oral exposure source for wildlife and populations lacking safely managed drinking water, the intrinsic biological effects of HA and FA after chronic oral exposure remain insufficiently understood. Here, we conducted a 90-day multidose oral mouse exposure integrating histopathology, biochemistry, gut microbiome profiling, and untargeted metabolomics to evaluate responses to Suwannee River humic acid (SRHA) and fulvic acid (SRFA). Both substances were associated with lipid-related metabolic alterations, intestinal mucosal changes, neural alterations, and oxidative-stress-related responses. SRHA, with higher aromaticity and apparent molecular weight, showed broader gut microbial changes, whereas SRFA, with lower apparent molecular weight and higher polarity, showed broader metabolic alterations in serum, liver, and brain. Multiomics integration revealed distinct microbiota–metabolome associations, while complementary interface assays suggested that structural and interfacial differences may contribute to these response patterns. These findings demonstrate distinct biological responses to chronic SRHA and SRFA exposure, supporting further consideration of the intrinsic bioactivity of humic substances in environmental exposure assessment.

articles.title: Fe–N x -Coordinated Algal Carbon with CaS for Enhanced and Extended Dechlorination of Chlorinated Hydrocarbons by Zero-Valent Iron
articles.abstract: Abstract Sulfidation improves the electron selectivity of zero-valent iron (ZVI), whereas Fe–Nx coordination structures could lower intrinsic dechlorination energy barriers. However, the synergistic integration of these two functionalities and their cooperative mechanism remain unclear. Here, we synthesized an algae-derived carbon material (Fex@NBC) containing both Fe–Nx sites and CaS via pyrolysis of iron-laden algal sludge. Upon coupling with nanoscale ZVI (nZVI), CaS-induced in situ sulfidation generated FeSx at the Fe0 surface, forming a dual-functional architecture with FeSx and Fe–Nx sites. The Fex@NBC/nZVI system achieved 84.3% of trichloroethylene (TCE) dechlorination within 24 h with a rate constant of 0.12 h–1 and an electron efficiency of 80.5%. Notably, 23.8% of the recalcitrant 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCA) was degraded within 50 days, demonstrating an extended dechlorination boundary. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Fe–Nx sites serve as the primary catalytic centers, while FeSx enhances interfacial electron transfer from Fe0 to Fe–Nx and suppresses hydrogen evolution. The cooperative regulation of catalytic activation and electron utilization remains effective under aging, ion influence, and realistic groundwater conditions. This work provides a resource-recovery concept for valorizing iron-enriched algal sludge while revealing the cooperative mechanism between Fe–Nx catalysis and FeSx-mediated electron regulation in ZVI-based remediation systems.

articles.title:
Precipitation-Modulated
Differential Scavenging of
Atmospheric Nitric Acid, Nitrogen Dioxide, and Particulate Nitrate:
Isotopic Constraints on Wet Nitrate Sources
articles.abstract: Abstract Quantifying the relative contributions of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and gaseous nitric acid (HNO3), and particulate nitrate (p-NO3–) to wet NO3– (w-NO3–) and understanding their differential scavenging remain critical challenges for nitrogen deposition modeling. Traditional approaches often neglect direct NO2 scavenging, introducing source apportionment uncertainties. Here, we compile a global dual-isotope (δ15N, δ18O) data set covering w-NO3– and its three precursors across 91 sites in Asia, North America, and Europe. Using an isotope mass-balance model, we quantify fractional contributions (F values) and preferential scavenging degrees (β values) of each precursor and examine their responses to mean annual precipitation. Average F values for NO2, HNO3, and p-NO3– are 26 ± 18, 39 ± 20, and 35 ± 20%, respectively, while their atmospheric abundance fractions (f values) are 76 ± 12, 9 ± 7, and 15 ± 11%. β values follow a universal order (βHNO3 > βp-NO3– > βNO2), confirming that HNO3 is preferentially scavenged. Precipitation modulates β values species-specifically: βHNO3 decreases with increasing precipitation, whereas βNO2 increases. Notably, our results suggest a tentative shift toward p-NO3– as the dominant precursor of w-NO3– at roughly 1750 mm of mean annual precipitation, although this crossing does not represent a statistically robust threshold. These findings provide quantitative constraints for model parametrization and inform region-specific nitrogen mitigation strategies.

articles.title:
Nationwide Study
of Per-and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances
in Dragonfly Larvae and Water in United States Protected Areas
articles.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widespread in the environment and are of global concern because of their prevalence, persistence, and toxicity. Information about PFAS on federally protected and Tribal lands is limited, despite calls from scientific and regulatory communities for data on environmental background concentrations. To respond to this, we leveraged an existing citizen-science network to collect dragonfly larvae (n = 179 sites) and water (n = 81 sites) from 108 national parks, national wildlife refuges, forests, and Tribal lands across the continental United States and Puerto Rico. Our results showed that PFAS are widespread, with PFOS and PFBA frequently observed (>60% of samples) in dragonfly larvae and water, respectively. Individual PFAS concentrations ranged from 0.22 to 56.6 ng/L in water and 0.10 to 480 ng/g dry weight in dragonfly larvae. Results from this novel broad-scale assessment indicated that concentrations were greater, and profiles were more diverse, in the eastern compared to western United States. Potential drivers of bioaccumulation were distance to source, habitat type, and land use, and large-scale variation in bioaccumulation was related to ecoregion and precipitation. Information from this study can help identify localized hotspots, prioritize monitoring and modeling efforts, and inform future management strategies.

articles.title:
A
Chain of Multiple Cryptic N-Fe-Mn-CH4 Redox Couplings
in Methanogenic Lake Sediments
articles.abstract: Abstract Approximately 30% of methane (CH4) emissions originate from freshwater sediments, typically oxygen- and sulfate (SO42-)-depleted, limiting their ability to regulate CH4 release. Here, we unravel a chain of triple cryptic N-Mn/Fe-CH4 redox couplings in natural, unpolluted reduced methanogenic lake sediments, which impact their cycles while sustaining complex aerobic and anaerobic microbial communities. Sediment profiles revealed an unexpected increase in nitrite (NO2-) along with elevated Fe2+, Mn2+, active NC10 bacteria, and aerobic methanotrophs and decreased CH4 levels. Sediment incubations amended under anoxic conditions with labeled ammonium (15NH4+) produced 15NO2- and 15N2, indicating anaerobic NH4+ oxidation, likely coupled to Mn(IV)/Fe(III) reduction. We further identified a sink for NO3-/NO2- coupled to Fe2+ oxidation, with Fe2+ partly derived from Fe(III)-dependent CH4 oxidation. The activity of NC10 bacteria and Methylococcales suggests an additional NO2- sink via NO2- disproportionation and potentially dark oxygen production, thereby facilitating aerobic CH4 oxidation under anoxic conditions. These coupled cycles likely dominate sulfate-depleted, organic- and Mn/Fe-rich methanogenic freshwater sediments, including many eutrophic lakes and wetlands that are expected to expand under global warming.

articles.title:
Advanced
Classification of Light-Absorbing Aerosols
Using a Two-Dimensional Absorption Ångström Exponent (2D
AAE) Space
articles.abstract: Abstract Light-absorbing aerosols (LAA) play a critical role in climate forcing and remain one of the largest sources of uncertainty in climate models. Ambient aerosols exhibit complex absorption spectral features making the Absorption Ångström Exponent (AAE) calculation highly sensitive to the chosen wavelength range, which can significantly affect interpretations of aerosol properties and source contribution. This study introduces an advanced classification framework for LAA using multiwavelength absorption measurements and a two-dimensional AAE approach, strengthened by absorption deviation in UV (2D AAE + Δ340). For the first time, continuous field measurements at seven European sites using a new nine-wavelength Aethalometer (AE36s; 340–950 nm) were combined with targeted laboratory experiments to systematically characterize aerosol absorption properties. AAE was calculated over two spectral ranges, AAE400–590 (400, 470, 520, 590 nm) and AAE590–950 (590, 630, 880, 950 nm) and the relative deviation at 340 nm from the AAE400–590-derived power law fit (Δ340) was introduced as an additional metric. The resulting 2D AAE fingerprints enable robust discrimination among fresh and aged black carbon (BCfresh, BCaged), residential and open biomass-burning aerosol (BBres and BBopen), and mineral dust. The proposed 2D AAE approach significantly improves LAA type identification and source apportionment compared with conventional single-range AAE analysis, enhancing interpretation of multiwavelength absorption data and supporting more accurate assessment of aerosol climate and air-quality impacts.
